recipes.name: Delicious Easy Chicken Francese
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast halves
2 tablespoons olive oil, or as needed

steps.text: Dredge chicken in flour; shake off excess. Dip into beaten egg. Lift up so excess egg drips back into the bowl. Press into flour again to coat both sides. Repeat with remaining chicken.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add chicken and sauté until almost cooked through, about 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate.
Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Heat chicken broth, wine, butter, lemon juice, parsley, salt, and pepper in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until butter melts. Stir water and cornstarch together in a small bowl until combined; add to broth mixture and cook until it thickens slightly, 2 to 3 minutes.
Place chicken into the prepared baking dish and pour sauce over top.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 10 to 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Easy Chicken Francese
raw_recipe.description: This easy chicken francese recipe features lightly battered chicken that’s baked with a buttery mixture of lemon juice, fresh herbs, and wine.

review.reviewBody: This was a big hit. Yummy Yummy. I did have to change a few things around. I also ready from the person who originally wrote it that there was a type so pay attention to that. I had 2 very big boneless breasts that I cut thru the middle to make 4 thin pieces of chix. I don't really know the weight for the chicken I used. I did juice from one good size lemon and used only 1 1/2 cups of chix broth. When I made my cornstarch mixture...it was a good 4 teaspoons mixed with 4-5 teaspoons of water. I didn't bake anything. I just made the sauce. Seared the chicken. Than added sauce to chick pan and put on low with cover on until done. OH SO YUMMY!!!!
Added chicken back to the skillet in the sauce and covered on low to finish and then added fresh spinach. Served with roasted new potatoes and sugar snap peas.
This was easy and excellent! I used 3 thin, boneless breasts, so I halved the eggs (used 2 not 4), broth, wine and lemon juice. Next time, I will only bake them for 10 minutes, not 15.

I rarely thicken with corn starch as it breaks down if you have left overs. Instead, try Rice flour! It holds up better than corn starch or a flour thickener. Have to say my husband and I eat a LOT of chicken and this recipe will be added to our repertoire!

Turned out great, but like others have said, don’t bother with the oven and let it simmer in the pan with the chicken for 10 minutes. Fry the chicken in the pan, remove chicken to towel to drain oil and then mix ingredients in same pan to make sauce, then put chicken back, cover and sauté for 10 minutes. Also I used lemon juice instead of lemons at about 2-3 tbsps.

This was a pretty easy recipe to make. Like other reviewers, the sauce is a bit thin and I’d recommend adding more cornstarch when creating the sauce. To compensate for that, after putting it in the oven, I ended up pouring the sauce into a saucepan, adding more cornstarch, and cooking it down, then pouring it over the chicken again. Variations: Instead of chicken breasts, I used boneless thighs (I prefer dark meat). I seasoned the thighs prior to dredging to add more flavor (garlic powder, onion powder, coriander,seasoned salt, Italian seasoning). I also sautéed thighs in 3/4 coconut oil and 1/4 olive oil. Other than that followed recipe with cooking in stove first then putting in oven. Much better than other recipes I’ve tried.

The original poster likely had this baked in an attractive buffet dish for serving guests. For family meal finishing all in skillet works. Personally, I do not measure dredging ingredients, I’d begin .with one jumbo egg! The cornstarch slurry can be omitted as the flour on the chicken will help thicken the sauce and I cut down the sauce ingredients to 1/2 of each the broth, wine, juice & butter. Too much liquid makes for a poached texture which I do not care for. This is also great served with a rice pilaf and steamed or roasted green vegetables.

I thought it was delicious. I did salt and pepper the chicken breast before I added to egg and flour and they came out excellent, tender and flavorful. The sauce did not thicken up too much, but I did like it this way. You would need to add more corn starch to thicken up.

I have this recipe bookmarked on my phone. I made this recipe once a week all throughout my pregnancy, and I'm still making it now. I find that I only need to use one egg and about 2 Tbsp. flour. I never use any less lemon than is called for. The tanginess is great. I specifically use dry Sherry for the white wine. This is great over the microwavable orange colored package of brown rice/ quinoa blend with garlic flavor that you can find at most grocery stores and Costco these days. I also make creamed spinach on the side. The sauce of this recipe is very soupy, which I like, but it is best to leave the creamed spinach or whatever veggie side we have in a separate dish.
Excellent recipe. I read the reviews and made the chicken on the stove like I do Chicken Marsala. This came out so tender and delicious. Thank you!

This recipe is insane. The whole family went nuts over it. Even my picky 5 and 2 years old went nuts with a little Parm cheese on top, yum. I've never eaten this dish out anywhere let alone make it. I was not at all disappointed. I did make few adjustments as other users suggested. I used 1 egg and beat it with 1 Tbsp milk for the coating and there was plenty to do 4 skinless boneless thin chicken cutlets. It cut down on the egg taste, but still cooked and browned beautifully. I don't keep lemons on hand so I substituted 4 Tbsp lemon juice. I did end up using about 5 tsp cornstarch mixed with 5 tsp water to get the sauce to thicken right, but remember as the sauce cools it does slightly thicken. I added garlic to the sauce as well. I did not bake this dish I opted to dirty several dishes on the stove top instead. I sauted the chicken with 1 Tbsp olive oil and just kept turning it. When it was almost cooked I turned the heat down. It came out very moist this way. I made my sauce in a separate pan. I also used other suggestions to serve with angel hair pasta and broccoli. I placed the pasta on each plate and dotted with butter, encircled the pasta with the broccoli, placed the chicken on top and then spooned sauce over the top of each one. It looked great and tasted even better. This recipe is a new family favorite!!

Should have read comments before making this dish. Need to use more cornstarch than recipe calls for. And, should have cooked mashed potatoes with our salads. My husband is Not a fan, but other than the thin sauce, it had a very good flavor!
Great recipe starter, easy to customize. Add others have noted, I also finished cutlets in the pan on low heat- no oven cooking in the summer!

A good basic recipe, and as many have said it needs more corn starch to thicken the gravy. There is no reason that this cannot be finished on the stove, by letting it simmer gently for 10-12 minutes and then add the corn starch slurry to thicken at the end. Use parsley or green onion for garnish. I added capers, lemon zest, some chopped spinach, and mushrooms. Test the sauce, if it's too tart a little sprinkle of sugar will balance it out.
I added lemons to the cooking dish and put capers in the sauce, delicious.
I added lemon pepper seasoning to give it that extra pop!
Easy to follow recipe simple to put together delicious sauce and chicken comes out perfectly. Great recipe.

I have been using this recipe for years its perfect the way it is but we like it more eggy if thats a word so flour than egg flour and egg again and a lot more fresh lemons thats my likings. just make sure you beat the chicken nice and thin. My kids love it!
Delicious I add some extra seasoning to the chicken before flouring and egging everyone loved it
This recipe was a huge hit. I will say I used more oil for frying the chicken pieces. Otherwise, the recipe was “right on”!
